title: Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report
description: Delaware Code Title 6 §2572 requires sellers of residential real property to deliver a completed Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report to the buyer. The report covers structural, mechanical, environmental, and material conditions. Sellers must disclose all known material defects. Buyer may rescind within 10 days of receipt.

required_actions.note: Buyer has 10-day right to rescind after receipt of the disclosure form.

title: Agency Relationship Disclosure
description: Delaware Code Title 24 §2913 requires licensees to provide written disclosure of agency relationships before any substantive discussion about specific property. Dual agency is permitted with informed written consent of both parties. Buyer's agents, seller's agents, and transaction brokers are all recognized relationship types.

required_actions.note: Must be provided before substantive discussions. Dual agency requires written informed consent of both parties.

title: Attorney-Required Closing State
description: Delaware is an attorney closing state. Delaware Supreme Court rules and state practice require that an attorney conduct the real estate closing, prepare the deed and settlement documents, and certify the title. Non-attorney settlement agents may not conduct closings without attorney supervision. Title insurance is standard.

required_actions.note: Delaware requires attorney involvement at closing. Attorney must supervise document preparation, title certification, and closing proceedings.

title: Realty Transfer Tax Disclosure
description: Delaware imposes a realty transfer tax of 4% of the property value (split 2.5% state, 1.5% county, with exemptions for first-time buyers under certain programs). 25 Del. C. §5401 governs the tax. Parties must disclose the allocation of transfer tax responsibility in the purchase agreement.

required_actions.note: 4% total realty transfer tax applies. Split is typically 2% buyer / 2% seller by custom, but negotiable. First-time buyers may qualify for partial exemption.

title: Delaware Lead-Based Paint Hazard Notification
description: In addition to federal requirements (42 U.S.C. §4852d), Delaware has its own Lead-Based Paint Hazards Prevention Act (16 Del. C. §2602 et seq.) which imposes additional requirements for properties built before 1978, including notification to occupants, disclosure during sale, and requirements for lead-safe work practices during renovation.

required_actions.note: Delaware imposes additional lead disclosure beyond federal requirements. Buyer has 10-day inspection opportunity.
